title: What Simon32/64 Neural Distinguishers Learn
summary: Observed Simon32/64 neural distinguishers perform similarly to but below one-fewer-round difference-distribution baselines; whether they only undo one unkeyed round and model differences remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{Simon32/64}$, observed $r$-round neural distinguishers achieve classification accuracy similar to, but lower than, $(r-1)$-round difference-distribution baselines. Determine whether an $r$-round neural distinguisher learns to decrypt one unkeyed round and then models only the resulting $(r-1)$-round difference distribution, learning no features beyond the distribution of differences.

scope.domain: Differential-neural cryptanalysis of Simon32/64, comparing neural distinguishers with difference-distribution baselines.
parameters: r: the neural distinguisher's round count, with r minus one rounds used for the difference-distribution baseline
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the neural distinguisher only decrypts one unkeyed round and models the resulting one-fewer-round difference distribution, without learning features beyond differences.

progress.summary: The source states this as an explicit mechanistic conjecture motivated by Simon32/64 experiments comparing neural distinguishers with difference-distribution baselines. It provides no proof of the conjectured learned behavior.
citation_labels: Zhenzhen Bao et al., Enhancing Differential-Neural Cryptanalysis
